args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and review why it was promoted to production even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** after the latest deploy, all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release marked healthy in production. All three regions now run it. The service passes health checks and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Rolling back to v2.3.0 didn't need change-manager approval, since it has been healthy in production before.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the current health. It also lists two next steps:
  - Find out why v2.3.1 failed before it's deployed again.
  - Find out why it reached production even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
